chapter: Western University and Kansas City nightlife
title: Labor Day battle of the bands in Kansas City
summary: He recalls bands like Bennie Moten, Blue Devils, Trent and George E. Lee, and a later battle against Duke Ellington.

bands.name: Andy Kirk and His Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Yes, these were stocks--Jenkins' Music Store--was it Jenkins, in Kansas City? Or is that in Texas? Anyway, I went to that music store, and I bought those. So I saw Herschel (phonetic) after this Battle of Bands on Labor Day, you know; they had about eight bands there. Those bands start, I guess, about six or seven o'clock, and play up until two or three in the morning. And--
Do you remember any of the bands?
Oh, yeah. The boss was usually Bennie Moten.
Yeah.

Many days after Bennie died, well, Andy Kirk took it and ran away with it But Blue Devils was always bad. Southern Seranades was a powerful group. In those days, see, it was T. Holder instead of Andy Kirk. But Bennie was the boss then.
Yeah.
And--what's-er-name, Alphonzo Trent [illegible]? He was a powerful, new [illegible]--
Did he come up to play at this battle?
Sometimes, when he was available, but, see, he was mostly in Texas.
Yeah, he kept a steady job there.
Yeah, Adolphus Daffows (phonetic) Hotel.
By the way, my uncle was the head butler, the head bellboy at Adolphus Daffows Hotel.
Oh!
And, 'course George E. Lee, with that mighty voice, and later on, they had Thamon Hayes and his group. They were very exciting.
So these bands would really all be southwestern bands?
Yeah. Very few of the bands were from any other area, you know.
Yeah.

Now one time, I think--I don't know whether it was Kirk or Moten played out to Duke, but as usual, there was no contest. Now we played against-- opposite Duke one time. And as soon as we got through playing, we went over there and shook hands with Duke, even before they started, you know, (laughter) say, "you win." (laughter) Now this is the truth, it is with that band--
Which one are you talking of now?
That was the Jay McShann Maxan (phonetic) band of later years.
Oh, Maxine McShann.
That was when Blanton (phonetic) — Blanton was still with the band. But those--see, we've gone off on a tangent so far.
